A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RefracGS and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, novel-view synthesis, ablation, and water-removal experiments in Tables 1–3 and A1–A4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports WSGS comparisons and computational runtime breakdowns.

M1.justification: The neural height field, recursive intersection algorithm, normal interpolation, differentiable Gaussian tracing, and losses remain unchanged. Added grid settings and inference execution details document implementation; proposed temporal and alternative-representation extensions are future work.

E1.justification: The NeRFrac and RefracGS benchmarks and application tasks remain unchanged. Appendix E adds qualitative synthetic boundary cases involving near-water grazing views and submerged cameras (Fig. A3), extending the illustrated conditions without adding a benchmark.

E2.justification: WSGS is newly evaluated in Table 1 and Tables A1–A4, including the existing nine-view setting. All previous comparators, including the separate NU-NeRF failure comparison, are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 adds stage-level computation-time fractions evaluated separately for training and inference. Existing benchmark splits, resolutions, quality metrics, and training schedules remain unchanged; the newly stated grid and subdivision settings are implementation disclosures.

E4.justification: v2 adds computational bottleneck analysis in Appendix D.1 and qualitative boundary-case illustrations in Appendix E. The four component ablations, nine-view comparisons, and NU-NeRF failure analysis were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. The additional results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds WSGS PSNR values of 22.449, 20.868, and 17.915 for NeRFrac real, NeRFrac synthetic, and RefracGS, respectively; Tables A1–A4 add corresponding scene results. New runtime findings include subdivision accounting for 74% of training computation. Previously reported benchmark, ablation, and water-removal values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and the gradient derivations in Appendix B retain their mathematical content. Ray-direction, normal, and index symbols are renamed; the new limitations discussion explains constraints of the existing height-field formulation without introducing new formal assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same joint reconstruction, view consistency, quality, training-speed, real-time rendering, and editing contributions. The added comparator supplies evidence without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's brief radiometric and static-scene limitations, Section 5 and new Appendix E substantially expand applicability boundaries: single-refraction and height-field failures, grazing/submerged viewpoints, breaking waves, and limitations of 3DGS for exact geometry. They also discuss specific radiometric, temporal, and representation extensions. Section 4.2 newly attributes WSGS's weaker results to its planar-surface assumption.

D1.justification: Appendices B.1 and C.1 newly disclose a 200 × 200 proxy grid, two subdivision iterations, and approximate scene dimensions of 1.5 × 1.5 × 1 m. Appendix D.1 explains fixed-surface inference execution. Conversely, v2 removes v1's project-page link; this establishes an access-information loss, not that the resource became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to WSGS and NeuS. It positions WSGS as limited to planar water surfaces and mentions NeuS as a possible alternative scene representation. The remaining related-work coverage and central novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Localized edits update authors and affiliations, add keywords and acknowledgments, standardize mathematical notation, and introduce runtime and limitations appendix sections. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Fig. A3 and WSGS rows plus refractive-method markers in Table 1 and Tables A1–A4. Table 1 moves, and the supplementary layout and pagination change. Existing qualitative comparison grids are retained under renumbered captions.

improvement.justification: The WSGS comparisons, runtime breakdown, and explicit applicability limits make the existing evidence easier to assess, while the grid and subdivision details improve reproducibility. These are useful, bounded gains with unchanged core methods and existing scores. Removing the project-page link weakens resource discoverability but does not outweigh the added comparison and documentation.
